'''Ilja Rosendahl''' (born 23 February 1968) is a German film and music producer, director, screenwriter, actor, [[songwriter]], musician (vocals, guitars, bass) and voiceover artist.

==Biography==

===Artistic career===
Rosendahl was born in [[Bochum]]. He played in theater projects and sang in a rock band during high school. Since 1997 he has starred in feature films and TV series aired in the United States, Europe and Latin America.<ref name="Ilja Rosendahl Homepage">{{cite web|url=https://www.iljarosendahl.com|title=Ilja Rosendahl Homepage|accessdate=11 May 2018}}</ref>

In 2001 he started the American [[Electronic music|Electronic]] [[alternative rock|Alternative Rock]] solo music project [[Latent Anxiety]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] which has released 7 studio albums and garnered several awards. He also contributed vocals and guitars to the 2010 ''Mortal Loom'' album ''This Vastness''.<ref name="Latent Anxiety Homepage">{{cite web |url=https://www.latentanxiety.com |title=Latent Anxiety Homepage|publisher=Latent Anxiety |accessdate=14 April 2013}}</ref>

In 2021 he gave his debut as director and screenwriter of the short film ''Remaining Chance''.<ref name="Ilja Rosendahl Homepage" />

===Academic background===
Rosendahl holds a PhD and BSc in [[Natural Science]] with specialization in [[Radiobiology|Radiation Biophysics]], [[Cell biology|Cytology]] and [[Genetics]] and speaks 7 languages (German, English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, French, Russian).<ref name="Advances in Space Research Article 1">{{citation |title=Mutation induction in mammalian cells by accelerated heavy ions |journal=Advances in Space Research | publisher=Elsevier |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2005.03.067 |bibcode=2005AdSpR..36.1701R |volume=36 |issue= 9|pages=1701–1709|year= 2005|last1= Rosendahl|first1= Ilja M.|last2= Baumstark-Khan|first2= Christa|last3= Rink|first3= Hermann}}</ref><ref name="Advances in Space Research Article 2">{{citation |title= On the quality of mutations in mammalian cells induced by high LET radiations |journal=Advances in Space Research |publisher=Elsevier |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2006.11.034 |bibcode=2007AdSpR..40..474B |volume=40 |issue= 4|pages=474–482|year= 2007|last1= Baumstark-Khan|first1= Christa|last2= Rosendahl|first2= Ilja M.|last3= Rink|first3= Hermann}}</ref><ref name="The Smithsonian/NASA Astrophysics Data System Abstract 1">{{citation |title=Mutation induction in mammalian cells by accelerated heavy ions |journal= Advances in Space Research|bibcode=2005AdSpR..36.1701R |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2005.03.067 |volume=36 |issue= 9|pages=1701–1709|year= 2005|last1= Rosendahl|first1= Ilja M.|last2= Baumstark-Khan|first2= Christa|last3= Rink|first3= Hermann}}</ref><ref name="The Smithsonian/NASA Astrophysics Data System Abstarct 2">{{citation |title=On the quality of mutations in mammalian cells induced by high LET radiations |journal= Advances in Space Research|bibcode=2007AdSpR..40..474B |doi=10.1016/j.asr.2006.11.034 |volume=40 |issue= 4|pages=474–482|year= 2007|last1= Baumstark-Khan|first1= Christa|last2= Rosendahl|first2= Ilja M.|last3= Rink|first3= Hermann}}</ref>
